issue_context.title: Integer overflow in apps/speed.c
issue_context.body:
In speed.c, the option `multi` can be specified through command line:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/0ad7578822b188447b1946e65a0ec4b5b07ead3f/apps/speed.c#L1592

The value of `multi` is not sanitized and passed directly into `do_multi`:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/0ad7578822b188447b1946e65a0ec4b5b07ead3f/apps/speed.c#L1809

which is then used as size for memory allocation:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/0ad7578822b188447b1946e65a0ec4b5b07ead3f/apps/speed.c#L3472.

By specifying `multi` (e.g., making it very large), one can trigger a signed integer overflow during the computation of the allocation size, which is a bug and can be dangerous.
comments:
The openssl command line tools aren't installed with any privilege and running speed from another application that could inject a large value seems unlikely.  I'm failing to see the danger here.  Moreover, there is only a problem is int and size_t are the same size, for most 64 bit machines this isn't true.

I agree that this is a bug.
Huh?  `app_malloc` takes a size_t: `void *app_malloc(size_t sz, const char *what);`  It did in 1.1.1 as well.  Earlier versions are unsupported.

I was looking at the branch OpenSSL_1_1_1-stable (link to the [code](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/OpenSSL_1_1_1-stable/apps/apps.c#L955)).
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/0ad7578822b188447b1946e65a0ec4b5b07ead3f/apps/apps.c#L955

`app_malloc` takes an `int`. Am I missing something here?

I must have been in the wrong place....
Yes, this is a different problem in 1.1.1.
A 1.1.1 PR will need to be raised once this has been reviewed.

review_comments: perhaps a comment here explaining why you do the divide is a good idea?
There isn't such a comment in the equivalent code in master or 3.0 :)
